newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Jan 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Jan 30.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- TOYOTA CHIEF IN WARNING ON EMU

Japanese automotive giant Toyota, one of the biggest foreign investors in the UK, has warned that delays or even non-entry by Britain to European monetary union could force the company to change its strategy on European investment. The warning is an embarrassment to the government, which has been trying to highlight its record on attracting investment to the UK. A Downing Street statement sought to play down the comments by suggesting that Toyota was not planning any additional investments in Britain.
-- PRU OFFERS STRATEGY TALKS WITH ITS PORTFOLIO

Prudential Corp, the UK investment giant, has established a mechanism for companies in which it invests to enable them to hold advance discussions on possible deals or strategy shifts. In an interview with the Financial Times, Derek Higgs, chairman of Prudential Portfolio Managers, the Pru's fund management arm, outlined details of the consultation mechanism, and he also issued a call for companies to secure shareholder approval for political donations.
-- BSKYB TO LAUNCH DIGITAL SATELLITE TELEVISION

Satellite broadcaster British Sky Broadcasting is to proceed with the launch of digital satellite television in the UK, leading to the arrival of up to 200 television channels in Britain by the end of 1997. BSkyB is drawing up formal documents to order one million set-top decoders needed to receive the service. The order, expected to be worth 250 million stg, is understood to have been completed 'in all but detail' with four manufacturers, thought to be Pace Micro-electronics, Panasonic, Sony and Nokia.
-- OLIVETTI FORECASTS $497 MLN LOSSES

Troubled Italian information technology group Olivetti has emphasised that it faces a more stable future, despite announcing an estimated pre-tax loss for 1996 at about 800 billion lire ($497 million). A board meeting to review the preliminary 1996 results confirmed the optimistic outlook offered by the strategy to dispose of the loss-making PC division and to concentrate on telecoms, information technology solutions and services, and office products.
-- FIAT'S IVECO TO CLOSE LANGLEY TRUCK PLANT

Italian automotive group Fiat is to close the truck plant at Langley, Staffordshire, of its commercial vehicles arm Iveco. An announcement on the closure, which will entail the loss of about 500 jobs, is expected next month. The Langley plant makes Britain's best-selling truck, the Cargo, which is a joint venture between Iveco and Ford. The closure of the plant will increase tension between Ford and its unions, following the announcement of 1,300 job losses at the company's Halewood plant on Merseyside earlier this month.
-- LONDON CLEARS $10 BILLION WORTH OF GOLD DAILY

The London Bullion Market Association has given the first authoritative indication of the size of the global gold market by revealing that deals involving about 30 million troy ounces, or 930 tonnes, of gold valued at more than $10 billion (6 billion stg) are cleared every working day in London. The London daily volume is almost double South Africa's annual production, and is equivalent to European Union central banks' reserves.
-- TWO BILLION STG LOST TO CORPORATE TAX AVOIDANCE

A senior government working party set up to investigate the shortfall in public finances has reported that tax planning and avoidance by companies cost the UK two billion stg last year. The findings of the report, which resulted from an inquiry by the Treasury and Customs & Excise, were published by the National Audit Office on Wednesday. The report also reveal a shortfall of five billion stg in VAT receipts on forecasts made two years ago.
-- BRUSSELS TO PROBE BT-MCI DEAL

Sources close to the European Commission have indicated there is 'every chance' that it will launch a detailed probe into the proposed merger between British Telecom and US long-distance telephone carrier MCI. An announcement on the inquiry is expected Thursday, although the Commission is thought to be unlikely to raise any serious objections to the 12 billion stg deal. Separately, the UK telecoms regulator Don Cruickshank has said the proposed merger would be 'an entirely desirable development'.
-- PREMIER FARNELL ISSUES PROFITS WARNING

Electronic components distributor Premier Farnell has warned that annual pre-tax profits for the year to February will fall up to eight percent short of forecasts. Shares in the company fell 59.5p to 632.5p on the news, which comes less than 12 months after Farnell's controversial 1.85 billion stg takeover of a US group. The company blamed the strength of sterling as well as weak market conditions in US and UK for the poor performance.
-- MICHELIN LOOKS AT US STOCK LISTING

European tyre maker Michelin is reported to be considering a US stock exchange listing. The French company is understood to be debating a possible move internally, with supporters of the idea claiming it would raise the group's profile in the significant North American market. A growing number of French companies have sought a US listing, and Michelin already has a strong international business, with just 20 percent of the group's 1995 turnover coming from the domestic market in France.
